title: Let Opus plan while a cheap model writes the code
summary: A developer built Cheap Agent so Claude Code's Opus plans and a cheap model writes test-proven code; he reports 63% fewer Opus tokens on one feature.
model: Claude Opus 5.5, DeepSeek and other cheap models
agent_role: Opus plans and splits the work; a cheap model writes code and a test in a separate copy of the project; Sonnet takes over failed steps; the human reviews the uncommitted changes.
outcome: Author reports 154k vs 57k Opus tokens on the same feature, and native Windows support built in 30 cheap-model jobs for $0.29 total.
what_they_did: The developer added a connector to Claude Code. Opus writes a plan, then hands each step to a cheap model in a private copy of the project. The cheap model must write a test that fails before its fix and passes after. Only passing work lands, uncommitted, for the human to review.
how_it_went: He reports his plan lasts 2.2 to 2.7 times longer. On the hardest test bugs it solved 6 of 9 versus 7 for plain Opus. Small jobs saw no savings.
worth_knowing: Your code is sent to the cheap model's provider once you allow it per project. Savings show up mainly on mid-sized features, not tiny edits.
prompt: For this task in [my project], act as the planner only. Write a step-by-step plan and, for each step, a test that should fail now and pass once done. Hand each step to [cheap model via my configured provider] to write the code. Run the tests yourself and only accept steps that pass. Leave all changes uncommitted, then show me a summary and the diff for review. Task: [describe the feature].

curation.rationale: Open-source tool whose README shows concrete measured workflows: a feature built with 63% fewer Opus tokens and Windows support built in 30 cheap jobs for $0.29, plus honest benchmark caveats.
